sentences.zh: 有义务告诉那些在谷歌搜索这些组合搜索词的人：听着，你可能

sentences.zh: 真的需要去检查一下了。

sentences.en: Seth Stevens-Dividowicz is a former data scientist at Google and the author of
sentences.zh: 赛斯·斯蒂芬斯-达维多维茨是谷歌的前数据科学家，也是

sentences.en: the book, Everybody Lies, Big Data, New Data, and What the Internet Can Tell Us About Who We Really Are.
sentences.zh: 《人人都在说谎：大数据、新数据以及互联网能告诉我们我是谁》一书的作者。

sentences.en: Seth, thank you for joining me today on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 赛斯，谢谢你今天来到我们的“隐藏大脑”节目。

sentences.en: Thanks so much for having me, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我，尚卡尔。

sentences.en: Have you ever talked to your computer, cursed it for making a mistake?
sentences.zh: 你有没有跟你的电脑说过话，咒骂它犯了错？

sentences.en: PC load letter?
sentences.zh: 打印机缺纸？

sentences.en: What the f*** does that mean?
sentences.zh: 这他妈到底是什么意思？

sentences.zh: 你有没有跟谷歌地图或 Waze 提供的行车路线争吵过？

sentences.en: Starting route to Grover's Mill Road.
sentences.zh: 开始规划前往格罗弗斯米尔路的路线。

sentences.en: Have you ever looked at a Roomba cleaning the floor on the other side of the room and told it,
sentences.zh: 你有没有看着房间另一头的 Roomba 机器人清扫地板，然后对它说：

sentences.en: please come over to this side.
sentences.zh: 请到这边来。

sentences.en: Turn left.
sentences.zh: 向左转。

sentences.en: Left!
sentences.zh: 左边！

sentences.en: It just ran itself right over the edge.
sentences.zh: 它直接从边缘冲下去了。

sentences.en: Robots and artificial intelligence are playing an ever-larger role in all of our lives.
sentences.zh: 机器人和人工智能在我们所有人的生活中扮演着越来越重要的角色。

sentences.en: Of course,
sentences.zh: 当然，

sentences.en: this is not the role that science fiction once imagined.
sentences.zh: 这并不是科幻小说曾经想象的角色。

sentences.en: It doesn't feel pity or remorse or fear.
sentences.zh: 它没有同情心、没有愧疚感、也没有恐惧。

sentences.en: Robots bent on our destruction remain the stuff of movies like Terminator.
sentences.zh: 一心想要毁灭我们的机器人依然只是《终结者》这类电影里的东西。

sentences.en: And robot sentience is
sentences.zh: 而机器人的感知能力

sentences.en: still an idea that's far off in the future.
sentences.zh: 仍然是一个遥远的未来概念。

sentences.en: But there's a lot we're learning about smart machines,
sentences.zh: 但关于智能机器，我们正在了解很多，

sentences.en: and there's a lot that smart machines are teaching us about how we connect with the world around us
sentences.zh: 智能机器也在很大程度上教导我们如何与周围的世界

sentences.en: and with each other.
sentences.zh: 以及彼此建立联系。

sentences.en: My guest today has spent a lot of time thinking about how we interact with smart machines
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾花了很多时间思考我们如何与智能机器互动，

sentences.en: and how those interactions might change the way we relate to one another.
sentences.zh: 以及这些互动将如何改变我们彼此关联的方式。

sentences.en: Kate Darling is a research specialist at the MIT Media Lab.
sentences.zh: 凯特·达林是麻省理工学院媒体实验室的研究专家。

sentences.en: She joined us recently in front of a live audience at the Hotel Jerome in Aspen, Colorado,
sentences.zh: 她最近在科罗拉多州阿斯彭的热罗姆酒店，

sentences.en: as part of the Aspen Ideas Festival.
sentences.zh: 作为阿斯彭思想节的一部分，与现场观众进行了交流。

sentences.en: Also on stage was a robot, a green robot dinosaur about the size of a small dog
sentences.zh: 台面上还有一个机器人，一只小狗大小的绿色恐龙机器人，

sentences.en: known as a pleo.
sentences.zh: 名叫 Pleo。

sentences.en: It's going to be part of this conversation.
sentences.zh: 它将成为这场对话的一部分。

sentences.en: But before we get to that, here's Kate.
sentences.zh: 但在我们开始之前，有请凯特。

sentences.en: Kate, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 凯特，欢迎来到“隐藏大脑”。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我。

sentences.en: You found that there is an interesting point in the relationship between humans and machines.
sentences.zh: 你发现人类与机器的关系中存在一个有趣的转折点。

sentences.en: And that point comes when we give a machine a name.
sentences.zh: 而这个转折点出现在我们给机器起名字的时候。

sentences.en: I understand that you have three of these pleo dinosaurs at your home.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，你家里有三个这样的 Pleo 恐龙。

sentences.en: Can you tell me some of the names that you have given to your robots?
sentences.zh: 能告诉我你给你的机器人起了一些什么名字吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 可以。

sentences.en: So the very first one I bought, I named Yochai after Yochai Benkler, who's a Harvard professor
sentences.zh: 我买的第一个机器人，我给它起名叫约查伊，以此向约查伊·本克勒致敬，他是一位哈佛教授，

sentences.en: who's done some work in intellectual property and other areas that I've always admired.
sentences.zh: 在知识产权和其他我一直很钦佩的领域做过一些研究。

sentences.en: And the second one I adopted after I filmed a Canadian documentary where the show host had to name the robot.
sentences.zh: 第二个是我在拍摄一部加拿大纪录片后收养的，当时节目主持人必须给机器人起个名字。

sentences.en: And he gave the robot the same name he had, which was Peter.
sentences.zh: 他给机器人起的名字和他自己的一样，叫彼得。

sentences.en: So the second one has a boring name.
sentences.zh: 所以第二个名字很无聊。

sentences.en: And then the third one is named Mr. Spaghetti.
sentences.zh: 第三个名字叫“意大利面条先生”。

sentences.en: I don't know if people outside of Boston are familiar with this,
sentences.zh: 我不知道波士顿以外的人是否熟悉这个，

sentences.en: but the Boston public transportation system, they wanted to crowdsource a name for their mascot dog.
sentences.zh: 但波士顿的公共交通系统当时想通过众包方式为他们的吉祥物狗征集一个名字。

sentences.en: And the internet decided that the dog should be named Mr. Spaghetti.
sentences.zh: 而互联网决定给这只狗命名为“意大利面条先生”。

sentences.en: And of course, they refused to do that and named the dog Hunter.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们拒绝了这样做，而是给这只狗取名叫亨特。

sentences.en: So Mr. Spaghetti became a big thing in Boston for a while.
sentences.zh: 所以斯帕盖蒂先生在波士顿火了一阵子。

sentences.en: People were very outraged about this.
sentences.zh: 人们对此感到非常愤怒。

sentences.en: And so I named my pleo, my third one, Mr. Spaghetti.
sentences.zh: 所以我把我的第三只Pleo恐龙玩具命名为斯帕盖蒂先生。

sentences.en: I understand that companies actually have found that if you sell a robot with the name of the robot on the box,
sentences.zh: 据我了解，一些公司实际上发现，如果销售一个机器人在包装盒上印上名字，

sentences.en: it changes the way people will interact with that robot than if you just said, this is a dinosaur.
sentences.zh: 比起仅仅说这是一个恐龙，它会改变人们与该机器人互动的方式。

sentences.en: So this is, yeah, this is not, I don't have any data on this.
sentences.zh: 所以这个，是的，这并不是，我手头没有这方面的具体数据。

sentences.en: But yes, I have talked to companies who feel that it helps with adoption and trust of the technology.
sentences.zh: 但确实，我交谈过的公司都觉得这有助于提升人们对该技术的接受度和信任度。

sentences.en: Even very, very simple robots like boxes on wheels that deliver medicine in hospitals.
sentences.zh: 甚至是非常非常简单的机器人，比如在医院里运送药品的带轮箱子。

sentences.en: If you give them a little nameplate that says Betsy, their understanding is that people are a little bit more forgiving of the robot.
sentences.zh: 如果你给它们挂上一个写着“贝西”的小名牌，人们对机器人的包容度就会高那么一点点。

sentences.en: So instead of this stupid machine doesn't work, they'll say, oh, Betsy made a mistake.
sentences.zh: 所以人们不会说“这台蠢机器根本不好使”，而是会说“哦，贝西犯了个错”。

sentences.en: And I'm wondering if you've spent time thinking about why this happens.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你是否花时间思考过为什么会这样。

sentences.en: At some level, if I came up to you at home and I said, Kate, is Mr. Spaghetti alive?
sentences.zh: 从某种程度上说，如果我走到你家对你说：“凯特，斯帕盖蒂先生是活的吗？”

sentences.en: You would almost certainly tell me, no, Mr. Spaghetti is not alive.
sentences.zh: 你几乎肯定会告诉我：“不，斯帕盖蒂先生不是活的。”

sentences.en: I assume you don't think Mr. Spaghetti is alive, right?
sentences.zh: 我猜你并不觉得斯帕盖蒂先生是活的，对吧？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So given that you know that Mr. Spaghetti is not alive, why do you think giving him a name changes your relationship to him?
sentences.zh: 那么，既然你知道斯帕盖蒂先生不是活的，为什么你觉得给他起个名字会改变你和他的关系呢？

sentences.en: With robots in particular, it's combined with just our general tendency to anthropomorphize these things.
sentences.zh: 特别是对于机器人，这结合了我们拟人化这些事物的普遍倾向。

sentences.en: And we're also primed by science fiction and pop culture to give robots names and view them as entities with personalities.
sentences.zh: 而且科幻小说和流行文化也让我们潜意识里愿意给机器人起名字，并将它们视为有性格的实体。

sentences.en: And it's more than just the name, right?
sentences.zh: 而且这不仅仅是因为名字，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, robots move around in a way that seems autonomous to us.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，机器人的移动方式在我们看来似乎是自主的。

sentences.en: We respond to that type of physical movement.
sentences.zh: 我们会对那种身体动作做出反应。

sentences.en: Our brains will project intent onto it.
sentences.zh: 我们的大脑会把意图投射到它上面。

sentences.en: So I think robots are the perfect mixture of something that we will very willingly treat with human qualities or lifelike qualities.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为机器人完美地融合了某种特性，让我们非常乐意以对待人类或生物的方式去对待它们。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So we have this wonderful little prop in front of us.
sentences.zh: 那么我们面前有一个非常棒的小道具。

sentences.en: It's a pleiodinosaur.
sentences.zh: 这是一只Pleo机械恐龙。

sentences.en: I want you to tell me a little bit about the pleiodinosaur, how it works, and how you come to own three of them, Kate.
sentences.zh: 凯特，我想请你跟我聊聊这只恐龙，它是如何运作的，以及你是怎么拥有三只的。

sentences.en: What is the dinosaur?
sentences.zh: 这只恐龙是什么？

sentences.en: What does it do?
sentences.zh: 它有什么功能？

sentences.en: It's basically an expensive toy.
sentences.zh: 它基本上就是一个昂贵的玩具。

sentences.en: I bought the first one, I think, in 2007.
sentences.zh: 我想我是在2007年买的第一只。

sentences.en: There we go.
sentences.zh: 你看，它醒了。

sentences.en: It's awake.
sentences.zh: 它醒了。

sentences.en: They have a lot of motors and touch sensors, and they have an infrared camera and microphones.
sentences.zh: 它们有很多马达、触觉传感器，还有红外摄像头和麦克风。

sentences.en: So they're pretty cool pieces of technology for a toy, and that's initially why I bought one, because I was fascinated by everything that it can do.
sentences.zh: 所以作为一个玩具，它们是相当酷的技术结晶，这也是我最初买它的原因，因为我被它能做的一切深深吸引了。

sentences.en: Like, if it starts walking around, it can walk to the edge of the table.
sentences.zh: 比如，如果它开始四处走动，它能走到桌子边缘。

sentences.en: It can look down, measure the distance to the floor.
sentences.zh: 它会向下看，测量到地面的距离。

sentences.en: Or it knows that there's a drop, and it'll get scared and walk backwards.
sentences.zh: 或者它知道前面有落差，就会吓得往后退。

sentences.en: And then they go through different life phases, adolescent and fully grown, and, you know, it'll have moods.
sentences.zh: 然后它们会经历不同的生命阶段，从幼年期到完全长大，而且你知道的，它也会有情绪。

sentences.en: So I think what we should do, we bought the robot at Hidden Brain a couple of weeks ago.
sentences.zh: 所以我想我们该做的是，几周前我们在《隐秘大脑》节目组买了这个机器人。

sentences.en: We haven't had a chance to give it a name yet.
sentences.zh: 我们还没机会给它起名字呢。

sentences.en: And I thought we should actually reserve the honors for this evening where we're talking to Kate and see if Kate wants to try and name this dinosaur, you know,
sentences.zh: 我想我们应该把这个荣誉留到今晚和凯特交谈的环节，看看凯特愿不愿意试着给这只恐龙起个名字，

sentences.en: since she cares about dinosaurs so much.
sentences.zh: 毕竟她那么喜欢恐龙。

sentences.en: I was looking up Kate's Twitter feed this morning.
sentences.zh: 我今天早上查了查凯特你的Twitter动态。

sentences.en: I understand that you're going to have a baby soon.
sentences.zh: 我听说你很快就要当妈妈了。

sentences.en: Congratulations.
sentences.zh: 恭喜你。

sentences.en: Yes, I don't have a name for that either.
sentences.zh: 是的，我连那个名字都还没想好呢。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Just FYI, she sometimes refers to the baby as Baby Bot, so just for whatever that's worth.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，她有时把宝宝叫做“机器人宝宝”，大家可以参考一下。

sentences.en: And one retweet that you had on your Twitter feed cracked me up.
sentences.zh: 你在推特上转发的一条内容让我笑喷了。

sentences.en: It said, you don't really know how many people you don't like until you start trying to pick baby names.
sentences.zh: 上面写着：“只有当你开始尝试给宝宝起名字时，你才知道自己究竟讨厌多少人。”

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a quote from my husband.
sentences.zh: 哈哈，那是我丈夫说的话。

sentences.en: So, I don't want you to tell me, you apparently haven't yet picked your baby's name, so do you have any choices, top choices?
sentences.zh: 所以，我不想问你——显然你还没给宝宝选好名字——那你有任何候选名字吗，最心仪的名字？

sentences.en: Is there a name, a spare name that you might care to give the dinosaur?
sentences.zh: 有没有哪个备用名字是你愿意送给这只恐龙的？

sentences.en: Well, the problem is we've had a girl's name picked out for years, and now we're having a boy, and we just can't, we don't even have any contenders.
sentences.zh: 嗯，问题是我们在几年前就选好了一个女孩名，而现在我们要生个男孩，我们简直连一个备选都没有。

sentences.en: No contenders.
sentences.zh: 一个备选都没有。

sentences.en: What would have been your favorite girl's name if you had had a girl?
sentences.zh: 如果你生的是女孩，你原本最喜欢什么名字？

sentences.en: Well, so, when I first started dating my now husband, he at some point said, if I ever had a daughter, I already know what I would name her.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是这样的，当我刚开始和我现在的丈夫交往时，他有一次说：“如果我以后有个女儿，我已经知道该给她起什么名字了。”

sentences.en: And I was like, oh, really?
sentences.zh: 当时我的反应是：“哦，真的吗？”

sentences.en: We're going to fight about this one.
sentences.zh: “我们得为这事争论一番了。”

sentences.en: And he said, yeah, I would name her Samantha and Sam for short, because Sam is kind of gender neutral.
sentences.zh: 然后他说：“对啊，我会给她起名叫萨曼莎，简称萨姆，因为萨姆听起来有点中性。”

sentences.en: And I was like, oh, I really love that.
sentences.zh: 我说：“哦，我真的很喜欢这个名字。”

sentences.en: So, that one was picked out very easily.
sentences.zh: 所以那个名字很快就定下来了。

sentences.en: All right, since you're not having a girl, you're going to have a boy, would you mind if you considered naming the dinosaur Samantha?
sentences.zh: 好吧，既然你生的不是女孩而是男孩，你介意考虑把这只恐龙命名为萨曼莎吗？

sentences.en: How would you feel about that?
sentences.zh: 你对此有什么感觉？

sentences.en: Oh, that would be awesome.
sentences.zh: 哦，那太棒了。

sentences.en: We should name the dinosaur Samantha.
sentences.zh: 我们应该把这只恐龙叫做萨曼莎。

sentences.en: All right, so, henceforth, this dinosaur will be called Samantha, or Sam for short.
sentences.zh: 好的，那么从今以后，这只恐龙就叫萨曼莎，简称萨姆。

sentences.en: Now, some time ago, Kate conducted a very interesting experiment with the Pleiodinosaurs.
sentences.zh: 话说不久前，凯特对Pleo机械恐龙做了一个非常有趣的实验。

sentences.en: And to sort of show how this works, I have a second prop here, which is under the table.
sentences.zh: 为了展示它是如何运作的，我这里第二个道具就放在桌子底下。

sentences.en: Uh-oh.
sentences.zh: 噢哦。

sentences.en: It's a hammer, a large hammer, which we borrowed from the hotel.
sentences.zh: 这是一把锤子，一把大锤子，我们是从酒店借来的。

sentences.en: Now, as you all know, the dinosaur is obviously not alive.
sentences.zh: 现在，正如大家所知，这只恐龙显然不是活的。

sentences.en: It's just cloth and plastic and a battery and wires.
sentences.zh: 它只是一堆布料、塑料、电池和电线的组合。

sentences.en: It has a name, of course, Samantha.
sentences.zh: 当然它有个名字，叫萨曼莎。

sentences.en: But it isn't alive in any sense of the term.
sentences.zh: 但在任何意义上它都不是活物。

sentences.en: And so, Kate, I'm going to actually give you the hammer.
sentences.zh: 所以，凯特，我要把这把锤子交给你。

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.zh: 哦，不要。

sentences.en: And I think we might have a little board underneath the table here.
sentences.zh: 我想桌子底下可能有一块小木板。

sentences.en: We're going to place the dinosaur on a board.
sentences.zh: 我们要把恐龙放在木板上。

sentences.en: Kate, would you consider destroying Samantha?
sentences.zh: 凯特，你考虑过毁掉萨曼莎吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: It's just a machine.
sentences.zh: 它只是一台机器。

sentences.en: I only make other people do that.
sentences.zh: 我只让别人做这种事。

sentences.en: I don't do it myself.
sentences.zh: 我自己可不做。

sentences.en: You wouldn't even consider harming the dinosaur?
sentences.zh: 你连伤害这只恐龙的想法都没有吗？

sentences.en: Well, so, my problem is that I already know the results of our research, and that would say something about me as a person.
sentences.zh: 嗯，问题在于，我已经知道了我们研究的结果，那会反映出我作为一个人的一些特质。

sentences.en: So, I'm going to say, no, I'm not willing to do it.
sentences.zh: 所以，我要说“不”，我可不愿意这么做。

sentences.en: Kate Darling is a research specialist at the MIT Media Lab.
sentences.zh: 凯特·达林是麻省理工学院媒体实验室的研究专家。

sentences.en: When we come back, I'll ask her about that research she references in which she asked volunteers to smash a robot dinosaur.
sentences.zh: 稍后回来，我会请教她关于她提到的那个实验，当时她让志愿者去砸碎一个机器人恐龙。

sentences.en: Welcome back to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到《隐秘大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: We're discussing our relationships with technology, specifically robots, with Kate Darling, a researcher from MIT.
sentences.zh: 我们正在与来自麻省理工学院的研究员凯特·达林讨论我们与技术的关系，特别是与机器人的关系。

sentences.en: She joined us before a live audience at the Aspen Ideas Festival.
sentences.zh: 她是在阿斯彭创意节的现场观众面前加入我们的。

sentences.en: A couple of years ago, Kate conducted an experiment that says a lot about how humans tend to respond to certain kinds of robots.
sentences.zh: 几年前，凯特做了一个实验，这很说明人类对特定机器人的反应倾向。

sentences.en: Tell me about the experiment.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲这个实验吧。

sentences.en: So, you had volunteers come up, and you basically introduced them to these lovable dinosaurs, and then you gave them a hammer like this, and you told them to do what?
sentences.zh: 所以，你让志愿者走上前，基本上向他们介绍了这些可爱的恐龙，然后你给了他们这样一把锤子，并让他们做什么？

sentences.en: Well, so, okay, so this was the workshop part that we used the dinosaurs for.
sentences.zh: 嗯，好吧，这是我们使用恐龙的工作坊环节。

sentences.en: They're a little too expensive to do an experiment with 100 participants.
sentences.zh: 用它们来做包含100名参与者的实验实在太贵了。

sentences.en: So, the workshop that we did in a non-scientific setting, we had five of these robot dinosaurs.
sentences.zh: 所以在非科学环境下的工作坊里，我们有五个这样的机器人恐龙。

sentences.en: We gave them to groups of people and had them name them, interact with them, play with them.
sentences.zh: 我们把它们分发给不同的小组，让他们给它们起名字、与它们互动、和它们玩耍。

sentences.en: We had them personify them a little bit by doing a little fashion show and a fashion conteSt.
sentences.zh: 我们让他们通过举行小型时装秀和服装比赛，赋予它们一些人格特点。

sentences.en: And then, after about an hour, we asked them to torture and kill them.
sentences.zh: 然后，在大约一个小时后，我们要求他们虐待并杀死它们。

sentences.en: And we had a variety of instruments.
sentences.zh: 我们准备了各种各样的工具。

sentences.en: We had a hammer, a hatchet, and I forget what else.
sentences.zh: 有一把锤子、一把手斧，我还记不清其他还有什么了。

sentences.en: But, like, even though we tried to make it dramatic, it turned out to be a little bit more dramatic than we expected it to be.
sentences.zh: 但是，尽管我们试图让它充满戏剧性，结果却比我们预期的还要戏剧化。

sentences.en: And they really refused to even hit the things.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至真的拒绝去敲打这些东西。

sentences.en: And so, we had to kind of start playing mind games with them.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不得不开始对他们玩起心理战。

sentences.en: And we said, okay, you can save your group's dinosaur if you hit another group's dinosaur with the hammer.
sentences.zh: 我们说：“好吧，如果你用锤子砸烂另一个小组的恐龙，你就能拯救你们小组的恐龙。”

sentences.en: And they tried, and they couldn't do that either.
sentences.zh: 他们尝试了，但还是做不到。

sentences.en: This one woman was standing over the thing trying, and she just couldn't.
sentences.zh: 有个女人站在那东西旁边尝试下手，但就是下不了手。

sentences.en: She ended up petting it instead.
sentences.zh: 最后她反而去抚摸它。

sentences.en: And then, finally, we said, okay, well, we're going to destroy all of the robots unless someone takes a hatchet to one of them.
sentences.zh: 然后，最后我们说：“好吧，如果我们不让一个人用手斧砍死其中一个机器人，我们要毁掉所有的机器人。”

sentences.en: And, finally, someone did.
sentences.zh: 最后，终于有人动手了。

sentences.en: Wait, so you said, unless one of you kills one of them, we are going to kill all of them?
sentences.zh: 等等，你是说你们当时说的是“除非你们其中一人杀死其中一只，否则我们要杀死所有恐龙”？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think this might have been my partner's idea.
sentences.zh: 我想这可能是我的搭档出的主意。

sentences.en: So, I did this with a friend named Hannes Gosselt.
sentences.zh: 我和一个叫汉尼斯·戈塞特的朋友一起做的这个。

sentences.en: We did this at a conference called Lift in Geneva.
sentences.zh: 我们在日内瓦举办的一个叫Lift的会议上做了这个实验。

sentences.en: And we had to improvise because people really didn't want to do it.
sentences.zh: 我们不得不即兴发挥，因为大家真的不想这么干。

sentences.en: So, we threatened them.
sentences.zh: 所以我们威胁了他们。

sentences.en: And, finally, someone did.
sentences.zh: 最后，终于有人动手了。

sentences.en: Samantha clearly doesn't want you to harm her.
sentences.zh: 萨曼莎显然不想让你伤害她。

sentences.en: Yeah, clearly.
sentences.zh: 对，显而易见。

sentences.en: Clearly.
sentences.zh: 显而易见。

sentences.en: So, what do you think is going on?
sentences.zh: 所以你觉得这背后的原因是什么？

sentences.en: I mean, at a rational level, the dinosaur obviously is not a lie.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，从理智层面来讲，恐龙显然不是活的。

sentences.en: Why do you think we have such reluctance to harming the dinosaur?
sentences.zh: 你认为为什么我们对伤害恐龙会有如此强烈的抗拒感？

sentences.en: In fact, I might have the battery removed so the dinosaur stops making noise.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我可能得把电池拆下来，免得这只恐龙一直发出噪音。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, it behaves in a really lifelike way.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，它的行为方式真的非常像活物。

sentences.en: I mean, we have over a century of animation expertise in creating compelling characters that are very lifelike,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们有一百多年通过动画塑造生动角色的经验，能创造出非常逼真的角色，

sentences.en: that people will automatically project life onto.
sentences.zh: 人们会不由自主地把生命投射到它们身上。

sentences.en: I mean, look at, you know, Pixar movies, for example.
sentences.zh: 你看，比方说皮克斯的电影。

sentences.en: It's incredible.
sentences.zh: 这太不可思议了。

sentences.en: And I know that a lot of social roboticists actually work with animators to create these compelling characters.
sentences.zh: 我知道许多社会机器人学专家实际上都在与动画师合作，以创造出这些引人入胜的角色。

sentences.en: And so, you know, it's very hard to not see this as some sort of living entity,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，你很难不把它看作某种有生命的实体，

sentences.en: even though you know perfectly well that it's just a machine,
sentences.zh: 尽管你心里非常清楚它只是一台机器，

sentences.en: because it's moving in this way that we automatically subconsciously associate with states of mind.
sentences.zh: 因为它运动的方式正是我们潜意识里会自动与精神状态联系在一起的。

sentences.en: And so, I just think it's really uncomfortable to people, particularly for robots like this that can display, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这真的会让人们感到很不舒服，特别是对于能够表现出痛苦或不适模拟状态的机器人，

sentences.en: a simulation of pain or discomfort to have to watch that.
sentences.zh: 要看着这种场景发生，

sentences.en: I mean, it's just not comfortable.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这真的让人很不舒服。

sentences.en: What did you find in terms of who was willing to do it and who wasn't?
sentences.zh: 从谁愿意动手、谁不愿意动手来看，你发现了什么规律？

sentences.en: I mean, when you looked at the people who were willing to destroy a dinosaur, a dinosaur like the pleo,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当你观察那些愿意毁掉一只恐龙（像Pleo那样的恐龙）的人时，

sentences.en: you found that there were certain characteristics that were attached to people who were more or less likely to do the deed.
sentences.zh: 你发现那些更有可能或更不可能下手的人身上有一些共同的特征。

sentences.en: So, the follow-up study that we did, not with the dinosaurs, we did with hex bugs,
sentences.zh: 所以我们后续做了一项研究，不是用恐龙，而是用微型六足机器人（Hexbugs），

sentences.en: which are a very simple toy that moves around like an insect.
sentences.zh: 那是一种像昆虫一样四处爬行的极其简单的玩具。

sentences.en: And there, we were looking at people's hesitation to hit the hex bug
sentences.zh: 在那里，我们观察人们对敲打六足机器人的犹豫程度，

sentences.en: and whether they would hesitate more if we gave it a name
sentences.zh: 以及如果我们给它起个名字，他们是否会更加犹豫，

sentences.en: and whether they would hesitate more if they had natural tendencies for empathy, for empathic concern.
sentences.zh: 以及如果他们天生具有同理心和共情关怀的倾向，他们是否会更加犹豫。

sentences.en: And, you know, we found that people with low empathic concern for other people,
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道的，我们发现那些对他人缺乏共情关怀的人，

sentences.en: they didn't much care about the hex bug and would hit it much more quickly.
sentences.zh: 他们对这个机器虫子没那么在意，动手拍打起来会快得多。

sentences.en: And people with high empathic concern would hesitate more and some even refused to hit the hex bugs.
sentences.zh: 而富有同理心的人则会犹豫更久，甚至有些人拒绝拍打这些机器虫子。

sentences.en: So, in many ways, what you're saying is that potentially the way we relate to these inanimate objects
sentences.zh: 所以，从很多方面来看，你的意思是，我们在潜在层面上与这些无生命物体的关系

sentences.en: might actually say something about us at a deeper level than just our relationship to the machine.
sentences.zh: 可能在更深层次上说明了我们的一些情况，而不仅仅是我们与机器的关系。

sentences.en: Yes, possibly.
sentences.zh: 是的，有可能。

sentences.en: I mean, we know now or we have some indication that we can measure people's empathy using robots,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们现在知道了，或者有一些迹象表明我们可以用机器人来衡量人们的同理心，

sentences.en: which is pretty interesting.
sentences.zh: 这挺有意思的。

sentences.en: You know, my colleagues and I were discussing ahead of this interview
sentences.zh: 你知道，我和同事们在这次采访前还在讨论

sentences.en: whether you would actually destroy the dinosaur.
sentences.zh: 你到底会不会毁掉这只恐龙。

sentences.en: And we were torn because we said on the one hand,
sentences.zh: 我们当时很纠结，因为一方面我们觉得，

sentences.en: you of all people should know that these are just machines
sentences.zh: 你最应该清楚这些只是机器，

sentences.en: and that it's an irrational belief to project lifelike values on them.
sentences.zh: 把栩栩如生的价值投射到它们身上是一种非理性的信念。

sentences.en: But on the other hand, I said, you know, it's really unlikely she's going to do it
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，我说，你知道的，她真的不太可能会这么做，

sentences.en: because she's going to look like a really bad person if she smashes the dinosaur in front of 200 people.
sentences.zh: 因为如果她在两百人面前砸碎这只恐龙，她看起来会像个大坏蛋。

sentences.en: I mean, I don't know if you've been watching Westworld at all,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我不知道你有没有看过《西部世界》，

sentences.en: but the people who don't hesitate to shoot the robots, they seem pretty callous to us.
sentences.zh: 但那些毫不犹豫向机器人开枪的人，在我们看来似乎相当冷酷无情。

sentences.en: And I think maybe there is something to it.
sentences.zh: 我想这或许确实说明了一些问题。

sentences.en: Of course we can rationalize it.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们可以为此进行合理化解释。

sentences.en: Of course, you know, if I had to, I could take the hammer and smash the robot
sentences.zh: 当然，你知道，如果非得这么做，我可以拿锤子砸碎这个机器人，

sentences.en: and, you know, I wouldn't have nightmares about it.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我不会因此做噩梦。

sentences.en: But I think that perhaps turning off that basic instinct to hesitate to do that
sentences.zh: 但我认为，或许关闭那种犹豫要不要动手的基本本能，

sentences.en: might be more harmful than, you know,
sentences.zh: 可能比……你知道的，

sentences.en: I think overriding it might be more harmful than just going with it.
sentences.zh: 我认为压抑这种本能，可能比顺其自然更有害。

sentences.en: I want to talk about the most important line we draw between machines and humans,
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈我们在机器与人类之间划定的最重要的一条界线，

sentences.en: and it's not intelligence, but it's consciousness.
sentences.zh: 它不是智慧，而是意识。

sentences.en: I want to play you a little clip from Star Trek.
sentences.zh: 我想放一段《星际迷航》的小片段给你们听听。

sentences.en: Now tell me, Commander, what is data?
sentences.zh: 现在告诉我，指挥官，什么是深蓝/数据？

sentences.en: I don't understand.
sentences.zh: 我不明白。

sentences.en: What is he?
sentences.zh: 他是什么？

sentences.en: A machine.
sentences.zh: 一台机器。

sentences.en: Is he?
sentences.zh: 是吗？

sentences.en: Are you sure?
sentences.zh: 你确定吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You see, he's met two of your three criteria for sentience,
sentences.zh: 你看，他已经符合了你关于感知能力的三个标准中的两个，

sentences.en: so what if he meets the third?
sentences.zh: 那么如果他符合了第三个呢？

sentences.en: Consciousness in even the smallest degree.
sentences.zh: 哪怕只有最微小程度的意识。

sentences.en: What is he then?
sentences.zh: 那他究竟是什么？
